theory.title: Patrones verbales con remember, forget, stop, try y regret
theory.explanation: Algunos verbos cambian de significado según vayan seguidos de gerundio (-ing) o infinitivo con to. Remember to do significa recordar una tarea pendiente; remember doing significa recordar una experiencia pasada. Stop doing es dejar una actividad; stop to do es detenerse para hacer otra cosa.
theory.tip: Fíjate en si hablas de recordar una experiencia o de no olvidar una tarea.

content.passage: When Nina arrived at the guest house, she remembered staying there years earlier with her grandparents. She stopped to speak to the owner, who still recognised her. Before going out, Nina remembered to collect a map from reception. She tried calling a friend, but the signal was weak, so she stopped using her phone and enjoyed the walk instead. Later, she said she would never forget visiting the village again.

items.prompt: Describe something you remember doing on holiday.
items.modelAnswer: I remember walking through a national park during a holiday in Wales. The path passed waterfalls and green hills, and we stopped several times to take photographs. It was a peaceful day, and I would love to go back.

items.prompt: What do you always remember to pack?
items.modelAnswer: I always remember to pack my phone charger, comfortable shoes and a light waterproof jacket. I also take a small bottle of water and any medicine I might need. These things make a trip more comfortable.

items.prompt: Have you ever stopped to ask someone for directions?
items.modelAnswer: Yes, I once stopped to ask a shop assistant for directions when I couldn't find the bus station. She explained which street to follow and pointed out a useful landmark. Her instructions were much clearer than the map.

items.prompt: Talk about a place you will never forget visiting.
items.modelAnswer: I will never forget visiting a small fishing village in Portugal. We arrived early, watched the boats return and had breakfast near the harbour. The people were friendly, and the place felt very different from a busy resort.

items.prompt: Describe a travel problem you tried to solve.
items.modelAnswer: During a city break, I couldn't use my bank card because the machine kept rejecting it. I contacted my bank and discovered that I needed to confirm the payment in the app. After that, I could pay normally.

items.prompt: What do you regret not doing on a previous trip?
items.modelAnswer: I regret not visiting the local art museum on my last trip. I thought I would have enough time on the final day, but our train was earlier than expected. Next time, I will plan museum visits before the last morning.

items.prompt: Explain the difference between stopping to rest and stopping working.
items.modelAnswer: Stopping to rest means taking a break during an activity so you can continue with more energy. Stopping working means finishing or pausing your job. For example, I stop to rest during a walk, but I stop working at six.

items.prompt: What should visitors remember to do in a hotel?
items.modelAnswer: Hotel guests should remember to leave the room key at reception if the hotel asks them to. They should also check the departure time and report any damage or missing items. It helps the staff prepare the room for the next visitor.

items.prompt: Talk about something you forgot to bring on a journey.
items.modelAnswer: Once I forgot to bring my sunglasses on a summer trip. The sun was very strong, so I bought a cheap pair at a local shop. Since then, I check my packing list before leaving home.

items.prompt: Recommend trying an activity in your area.
items.modelAnswer: I recommend trying a guided walk around the old part of my town. You can learn about the buildings, hear local stories and discover small streets you might miss alone. It is an enjoyable way to spend an afternoon.

content.audioTranscript: A: We are planning a trip next month. B: Where are you going? A: We are travelling to a historic town. B: Have you booked the journey? A: Yes, and we have printed the tickets. B: Which station will you use? A: The central one. B: Is there a local guide? A: Yes, we made a booking online. B: Do you know the platform? A: It is shown on the app. B: What will you visit? A: The museum and the market. B: Are you learning about local customs? A: Yes, and we are staying at a small hotel. B: Enjoy your arrival!
